A guide to the difficulty levels available in REX/M2EX.

REX/M2EX add a few new difficulty options.

- Fair difficulty sets bonuses for AI and the player to zero, and AI capabilities like hiring mercenaries are enabled, which leads to a level playing field.
- Extreme and Hell are tougher than the highest vanilla difficulty (Very Hard). Don't say we didn't warn you.

[This spreadsheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/12dUJozIRBn6Ln6LbyKeoc2vfsgHn4UEMv24WHMt4eJs/edit?pli=1&gid=0#gid=0) details the exact effects of every difficulty level in REX/M2EX.
A guide to configuring REX & M2EX.

REX and M2EX include a number of extra configuration options compared with the vanilla games.

## Main Menu Options
#### Graphics Settings
New options are available in the graphics options menu for some graphics settings (highlighted red in M2EX). For example the "Extreme" settings.

These push the graphical detail far beyond what the games were capable of before, *but can come at a significant cost to performance*. You can test these out and see what your PC can handle.

#### Modern WASD Control Scheme
In **Options** > **Keyboard Settings**, click the right arrow to change from "Total War Style Setup" to "FPS Style Setup".

## In-game options
While playing, you will find a number of new gameplay and graphical configuration options.

#### Unit Movement Run Mode
While playing, go to **Options** > **Game Options**.

This controls whether units walk (as in vanilla) or run. By default, this is set so they run when you drag out a formation.

#### New Camera and Tilt Options
While playing, go to **Options** > **Camera Options**.

By default, the **Camera Mode** is set to RTS Camera, which is REX/M2EX's much improved camera. 

Select **No Camera Tilt** if you want to disable tilting when you zoom in and out.

#### Unit cards and icons on highlight
While playing, go to **Options** > **Video Options**.

These determine if you see little icons and unit cards when you hold the highlight key (this defaults to space bar)

#### Unit Silhouettes
While playing, go to **Options** > **Video Options**.

This controls whether blue/red silhouettes of friendly and enemy units appear through obstacles, such as trees or terrain, enhancing visibility.

#### Range Indicator
While playing, go to **Options** > **Video Options**.

This controls whether a range circle is drawn around selected ranged units, showing how far they can shoot (depending on terrain etc).

This indicator can be customised further in the [Advanced Configuration Files](#advanced-configuration-files)

#### Blood Pools
While playing, go to **Options** > **Video Options**.

This controls whether pools of blood are created around dead soldiers.

## Advanced Configuration Files
Certain options are not currently available to tweak within the game. These can be found in text files in the `data` folder, such as: `descr_ex.txt` and `descr_caps_ex.txt`.

Note that these files will be overwritten every time you install a new release, so it's recommended to keep a note/backup of the values you changed and re-add them after upgrading to a new version.

Certain especially useful options are noted below (but the files have comments to explain each setting and what it does):

#### descr_ex
This section allows you to customise the look of the range indicators:
````
;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;
; Battle range indicator
;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;
````

A more subtle red range indicator configuration (closer to other Total War games) would be:
```
; Disc colour, r g b (0-255)
range_indicator_colour 255 0 0

; Alpha at the edge (0-1)
range_indicator_peak_alpha 1

; Alpha of the inside (0-1)
range_indicator_floor_alpha 0

; Inward fade width from the edge as a fraction of the radius (0-1)
range_indicator_falloff 0.015

; Outer-edge softness; small = crisp (0-1)
range_indicator_fuzz 0.008
```

`blood_pool_limit` allows you to set maximum [blood pools](#blood-pools) on the battlefield.

`corpse_limit` allows you to set how many corpses are allowed before the oldest ones are removed for performance reasons.

`show_unit_card_always` allows you to set [unit cards and icons](#unit-cards-and-icons-on-highlight) to appear at all times (and there are other options next to it allowing further customisation).

#### descr_caps_ex
`fog_of_war_shroud` - Allows you to change whether fog of war in REX is black or `vanilla` (grey).

`faction_unlock` - Allows you to change whether all factions are unlocked for the campaign straight away or revert to vanilla progression.

#### descr_sm_factions
You can use this file to add internal province borders on the campaign mini-map, by adding a `tertiary_colour` to each faction. 
![Campaign minimap showing internal province borders](../../../assets/minimap_internal_borders.png)

For example:
```
tertiary_colour                red 0, green 0, blue 0
```

#### Visibility of arrows
REX/M2EX makes arrows brighter than they are in vanilla by default.

`descr_projectile_new.txt` (REX) and `descr_flaming_projectiles.txt` (M2EX) allow you to customise this.

An example from the REX file for the parameters -

```
;<far> <mid> <length_cap> <whiten_cap> <whiten_gain>
distance_visibility    0.05 0.10 2.0 0.19 0.0007
```

If you would like to revert the look back to vanilla, set the "distance_visibility" lines in the files to:

`distance_visibility 0 0 1 0 0`

#### What exactly is REX/M2EX?
This project aims to patch Rome and Medieval 2, with the intent of modernising the game by making it 64-bit with DirectX 11 (instant alt tabbing ftw), fixing performance/stability issues, bugs & crashes, patching the hardcoded limitations out, adding features and giving modders the ability to modify the games further. 

It's not a mod, but a community patch that seeks to polish and improve without straying too far from the original vision of the developers. Think of it as if Rome and Medieval 2 had received another few years of development and patching by Creative Assembly, or as playing these games the way your nostalgia recalls them.

#### Main features
- A fully 64-bit engine, no 4GB limit (LAA no longer needed) and a new rendering backend
- Instant alt-tabbing and tons of small QoL additions
- Tons of crash fixes and bug fixes (way better stability)
- Improved the campaign AI a lot
- Massively increased performance (~5x more FPS is not uncommon) supporting huge armies without stutters and "extreme" graphics options for experimentation
- Lightning-speed end turn times and loading times (for AI spectator mode - 100 turns in 30 seconds)
- A fully modern, better RTS camera with fixed zooming, middle-mouse rotation and edge panning, zoom-in and zoom-out uncapped by a lot, and many other possible functionalities
- A fully rotatable campaign map camera
- Fully working alt-drag (also with ctrl pan drag) and unit card re-ordering (with units showing live kill count and prisoners captured during a battle)
- Fully working pikemen without sketchy fixes/removing their secondaries; fixed muskets/arquebusiers; fixed two-handers
- Improved multiplayer-like shared deployment, same factions on both teams
- STEAM DECK, LINUX and MAC support
- Improvements to the UI, such as range indicators for ranged units
- Removed every single major engine limit like factions, regions, religions, cultures, etc.
- Major expansion of modding tools
- Not one but *two* custom scripting APIs for new modding possibilities
- **Compatible with all OG mods**

But there are countless more, which you can find in the full changelog.

#### Are the roadmap and the features above a definitive limit on what can be achieved?
The sky is the limit! For the most part the true limit lies only in the number of people commiting to this project.

#### Who's in charge here? Who are the creators?
Aster and Pannoniæ founded the project, but the team has only grown since then. If you can commit to the project (anyone is welcome), you will be there too among the stars.

#### Why would I use REX instead of Rome: Remastered?
REX has already fixed more of the original game's bugs than the remaster, while avoiding some of the more controversial changes (such as to the UI, cutscenes, main menu and textures/lighting) which the remaster made and generally sticking closer to the original game in these respects. Unlike Rome: Remastered, REX is still in active development and has greater capabilities for modders too.

#### Are my old save games compatible with REX/M2EX?
Old vanilla save games will work on REX/M2EX.

However, saves made under REX/M2EX will not work on the original, unpatched games.

## I want to get involved

#### Is there a way to contribute to this project?
If you wish to contribute, you can contact either @Aster or @Pannoniæ or just hit up the [⁠applications channel](https://discord.com/channels/1456826444360581235/1489284562306596874) on Discord.

People with programming skills are very welcome, especially if you have experience with C++, but we don't just need developers. 2D/3D artists and other skill sets are also in high demand.

#### What can the non-contributors do?
Any support helps! Even if it's giving suggestions in the [⁠suggestions-rtw](https://discord.com/channels/1456826444360581235/1471288410332201011) and [⁠suggestions-med2](https://discord.com/channels/1456826444360581235/1471934523183861780) channels or reporting issues/bugs/crashes in ⁠issues, they're all appreciated! Also, feedback in [⁠feedback](https://discord.com/channels/1456826444360581235/1470746530683293726) matters, as do many other things like spreading the word or bringing more people into this project.

Separately, testing the test versions and providing feedback for them matters too - for test releases, check for the latest release described as a test release in [⁠releases](https://discord.com/channels/1456826444360581235/1471940087192227861) and then give some very appreciated input here [⁠feedback](https://discord.com/channels/1456826444360581235/1470746530683293726).

If you want to be pinged each time something good is up like a new test version - get the ping role here in [⁠faq](https://discord.com/channels/1456826444360581235/1471228372414631966/1518002786611101857)⁠. 

#### How do I suggest something and what is allowed?
Any suggestions are fine and I would strongly advise people reading the suggestions to not attack and massively vote down someone's suggestions, but at least try to have a conversation about why you'd think it's a good or a bad idea. As you are posting a suggestion remember to think about the amount of work your proposition may involve and the how much work is still to be done within this project. Also consider what is within the scope of this project and what is for e.g. for mods to do.

For example (not the complete list) it can be: an exploit to be removed, a vanilla bug to be fixed (a bug appearing without use of REX/M2EX), a gameplay change or there is something to be added or altered to make the game better.

You can submit your suggestions for Rome 1/REX in [⁠suggestions-rtw](https://discord.com/channels/1456826444360581235/1471288410332201011) and Medieval 2/M2EX in [⁠suggestions-med2](https://discord.com/channels/1456826444360581235/1471934523183861780). Remember that this is for suggestions, not bug reports. For that, head to this section of troubleshooting. 

## Safety and Legality

#### Is this malware?
No. We don't do anything like DLL injection (like EOP) , packing, obfuscation or other techniques you'd most commonly find in game cracks, this is just a bog standard .exe replacement. If your antivirus flags the .exe though, please let us know - that would be unusual and we'd definitely want to look into it.

#### Is this legal?/Is this safe?
You are fine. This is a community patch - we modify game files, not anything shady. Modding has been around forever and there's nothing unusual or risky about what we do. The EULA for both Rome 1 and Medieval 2 essentially prohibits 99% of modding, including simple texture swaps. We are on the same legal grounds and within the same established market practice as many mods (including those that have been around for over a decade).

If you've seen people claiming otherwise, it's most likely the same crowd that has spent years arguing about whether the 4GB/LAA patch is legal, and has been happy after receiving a non-binding company response that does not change the EULA situation and could be reversed at any time. But they are happy to discourage people by any means necessary, including lies, and avoid any discussion when met with counterpoints, just to see progress sink.

Outside the CA environment, people are doing far more extreme things with their games without issue, not to mention the most severe examples, such as the Far Cry 1 source code being on GitHub for years (Ubisoft is the IP holder). Also you can notice that Rome 1/Medieval 2 source code is available on the internet and nobody takes it down, just type on YT: "The 'Rome Total War' LEAKS" or "Solve ANY Rome Total War mystery with this video". Not to mention that many popular Rome/Medieval 2 mods use IP from Lord of the Rings, Warhammer fantasy etc and have done so for years now.

#### Should I be worried about all the "bug fix" entries in the changelog?
Nope. The majority of entries are just fixes for the original game, not a straight up sign of project instability. Most of these fixes (like the pikemen fix) were not doable up until REX/M2EX saved the day, and the longer this project goes on the more we find that needs fixing. 

Sometimes minor hiccups occur and it's 99% of the time dealt with quickly in a hotfix. Obviously it's a fan made project made in people's free time, after all.

## Modding

#### What is EOP? Which mod uses it?
EOP stands for Engine Overhaul Project. It is sort of a script extender that the newest Medieval 2 mods and their updates use. It's far less potent than M2EX, which can touch any aspect of the game directly, not just scripting and workarounds for the original game's quirks.

If you wonder which mods use EOP then simply Google it for the mod of your choosing, ask people playing it, its devs, or consult forums/Discord servers/mod pages. Be mindful that different versions of the same mod might or might not use EOP.

#### What is the difference between M2EX and EOP?
Basically, M2EX takes the engine code and upgrades it, porting it to 64-bit, adding a whole a lot of QoL features and so on as briefly listed above.

EOP instead takes the original 32-bit retail exe, starts it, pauses it then injects a bunch of code into it to extend the scripting features of the game with lua. This has its advantages/disadvantages but basically, it's a much more "roundabout" way of doing things with all the implications, including being much less potent that M2EX.

#### Is this compatible with EOP?
The newest releases include an implementation of EOP's API, and EOP mods are now compatible.

#### What is your stance on EOP?
We value how much EOP achieved while dealing everyday with painful workarounds and with much more restricted means compared to this project. We value the work done on EOP basis even if it had to deal with the problems mentioned above. We strongly welcome any cooperation with it if there are means to do it both on technical and personal level. However we acknowledge the fact that REX/M2EX simply gives much more in way convenient way to the players and the modders on almost every level - so we would like to move at steady pace in this direction while avoiding being held hostage to personal hiccups/drama if possible and responding to it when neccesary.

#### Why do so many mods use EOP?
Because it appeared way earlier than REX/M2EX.

#### What modding capabilities does this have?
Limitations on what can be modded are heavily lifted and still are being expanded such as with scripting, limits on factions/units/regions/etc are gone and in general there will be more options for modding/modding tools etc.

There are already mods which have been created expressly to work on REX/M2EX and take advantages of its new capabilities.

#### I am a modder and I want to use this gem of a project, what should I do?
Read the FAQ, consult the mods channel category, and if needed reach out for help in there or contact the project devs. Remember that this project changes many things, for example from a convoluted, buggy state to properly working so you may need to adjust certain things in your mod.

## Other

#### I am a content creator, can I count on any help?
Sure. Reach out to the community or the project creators. Just try being specific in your requests, be genuine and produce genuine content. Don't just be nagging for views. Reading the FAQ thoroughly, checking out what was added, fixed etc. in the ⁠changelog or looking at the bright future in ⁠roadmap will help you in knowing what to ask for and to produce good content in the end.

#### Why has this feature or that feature not been added yet?
The project is moving very quickly, but the amount of work involved in untangling and improving two games of this age is significant. There are a lot of ambitious feature requests, this is a project being done in people's free time, and the developers have to focus on stability and bug fixes as well as fancy new features. 

The fastest way to speed up progress is to [help out](#i-want-to-get-involved)!

#### How do I run AI only campaigns?
For REX add this into the target line in .exe properties `./REX.exe -ai -strat:imperial_campaign`

For M2EX the same but `./M2EX.exe --ai.debug=1 --misc.bypass_to_strategy=imperial_campaign`

#### How do I use CinEd for battle replays?
You put `[cine] show =1` your cfg or launch the game from a shortcut with `./M2EX.exe --cine.show=1`

#### How can I disable camera zooming in on gate breach/killed general, etc?
Go to the folder where you installed Medieval 2 and look for a file called `medieval2.preference.cfg`. 

Open it and in the [game] section, change 1 to 0 in the following line:
`event_cutscenes = 1`

#### Unit balance aka - You said pikemen, two handers and gunpowder units are fixed properly but they are now either way too OP or they are still useless. Why?
If they are too OP - mods or base game gave them way too good stats to boost them so the bugs won't bog their performance.

If they are useless or they underperform - simply some stats should get boosted.

In other words - stats were constructed around very different environment including bugs that even EOP could not fix but now REX/M2EX did. So it's rebalancing time!

If you think that the stats are fine and you still see any bug related to this matter like unit behaviour/mechanic/stats not working/whatever else - report it. Same goes for any suggestions for animations or something else getting adjusted to work properly. Just mind that if playing mods - some of them make deep changes into the animations or unit behaviour etc. and the mod devs should take note.

Mind that pikes specifically have to be handed well in battle, especially sieges affect their performance for good reason. Crowding mechanic, dispersion of the formation etc. might rightfully cause them to drop pikes. Also pathfinding is yet to be reworked and it is a factor.

#### I saw a feature in the ⁠changelog but it's not in the latest release. What gives?
To ensure stable builds, some changes might be pulled out for further refinement.

#### I am still confused, help!
If you are still confused about anything, have issues with the patch, or if you want to ask about whether anything is possible, try reading these guides again and using the Discord search bar, as many questions will have already been answered. You can refer to the [general](https://discord.com/channels/1456826444360581235/1469432655560048782) channel or relay any questions to the community or the original creators of this project.

If you are a new user, ask in [⁠newcomers-help](https://discord.com/channels/1456826444360581235/1511084305269653616) first for some help.
A guide to installing REX & M2EX.

### Prerequisites

- You **must** own the Steam version of Rome (original, **not** Remastered) or Medieval 2. If you have a CD/DVD copy, you can redeem a Steam copy using the CD key.
- Download and install from this link (the official Microsoft server) the latest [Visual C++ Redistributable](https://aka.ms/vc14/vc_redist.x64.exe) - the one coming with the games will not work.
- You do **not** need the 4GB/LAA patcher with REX and M2EX.
<Aside type="note">
  If you would like to keep a copy of the games without REX/M2EX, you can make a copy of the game folder somewhere and install REX/M2EX either in the original folder or in the copy.
</Aside>

### Installing

1. Find the latest "Stable Release" marked with a date in [Releases](https://discord.com/channels/1456826444360581235/1471940087192227861) on the Discord server. Don't download a "Test Release" unless you're ready for bugs! You can also download the latest GitHub version, but this may not always be as recent.
2. For Rome 1, download `REX.7z`. For Medieval 2, download `M2EX.7z`.

The following steps depend on your Operating System:

<Tabs syncKey="operating-system">
  <TabItem label="Windows">

    1. Extract all files to the game's root directory (**not** the `\mods` subfolder). This can usually be found in:
       - `C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Rome Total War Gold`
       - `C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Medieval II Total War`
    2. Replace any existing files when prompted.
    3. Run `REX.exe` for Rome 1 or `M2EX.exe` for Medieval 2. Don't run the games using Steam, as this will launch them without the patch!
  #### Notes
    - If you'd like to use the Steam overlay, you can add REX or M2EX to Steam as a Non-Steam Game
    - To launch the expansion packs for both games, use the below batch files in the REX/M2EX folder:

       | DLC | Batch file |
       | --- | --- |
       | Rome Total War: Barbarian Invasion | `Barbarian Invasion.bat` |
       | Rome Total War: Alexander | `Alexander.bat` |
       | Medieval II Total War: Kingdoms (Americas Campaign) | `Americas.bat` |
       | Medieval II Total War: Kingdoms (Britannia Campaign) | `Britannia.bat` |
       | Medieval II Total War: Kingdoms (Crusades Campaign) | `Crusades.bat` |
       | Medieval II Total War: Kingdoms (Teutonic Campaign) | `Teutonic.bat` |

    <Aside type="note" title="Alexander">

    Alexander is a seperate game on Steam. Copy the `alexander` directory from the Alexander installation folder into your REX/Rome installation folder. `Alexander.bat` won't launch Alexander if you don't do this first!

    </Aside>

  </TabItem>

  <TabItem label="Linux">

    1. Make sure to download the Steam **Windows** version. 
         - You can force this by going to Rome/Medieval 2's properties in your Steam library, selecting **force the use of a specific compatibility tool** -> **Proton 10.4** (needs to be a fairly new Proton version). If you have the Feral Linux port of Medieval 2 already installed, this will force a reinstall!
    2. Run the game once to make sure Proton works correctly.
    3. Extract all files to the root directory for the game (**not** the `/mods` subfolder).
    4. Replace any existing files when prompted.
    5. Add REX / M2EX as Non-Steam Games in Steam. Tell them to use Proton too (version 10 or later) with **properties** -> **force the use of a specific compatibility tool**.
    6. Launch REX / M2EX from your Steam library - it will crash but that's supposed to happen! (Steam will generate a new wineprefix, which you'll need for the next step).
    7. Launch ProtonTricks and select the REX / M2EX prefix. Choose the default prefix, then select **Install a Windows DLL or component**. Scroll down to `vcrun2022` and select its checkbox.

    <Aside type="note" title="Using ProtonTricks">

      If you have never used ProtonTricks, first make sure it is installed. When you launch it, ProtonTricks displays the Proton prefixes that Steam has created. Steam usually names each prefix after the corresponding game in your library.

      1. Select the prefix for REX / M2EX.
      2. Select **Select the default wineprefix**, then choose **OK**.
      3. Select **Install a Windows DLL or component**, then choose **OK**.
      4. Find and select `vcrun2022`.
      5. Choose **OK**, then close the remaining dialogs.

    </Aside>

    <Aside type="note" title="Steam Deck">

    All the steps are the same as above for Linux. The Steam Deck can run ProtonTricks in desktop mode to install `vcrun2022`. If you are not familiar with installing ProtonTricks for `vcrun2022` on SteamDeck check this guidehttps://pimylifeup.com/steam-deck-protontricks/.

    If you wonder how to apply a community-made control scheme for REX/M2EX - this is most efficiently done by just using an existing RTW or M2TW one.

    If you didn't like the UI and text scaling for Rome Remastered on this platform or you are simply afraid of it before trying - don't worry. The resolution on the original RTW and M2TW is great on the device. As a newcomer,  you will find that Total War games are fine to handle on the deck, broadly, due to the trackpads.

    </Aside>
  </TabItem>

  <TabItem label="macOS">

    You will need virtualisation software like Parallels
    You can install and run the game by following the Windows instructions on this page for the system within the virtualisation. 
    Other virtualisation software needs testing (we would appreciate any feedback on them), but CrossOver doesn't work.

    A to Z video about Parallels [here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n8pT_FwCmVA).

  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

### Uninstalling

If you'd ever like to remove REX/M2EX:
1. Find the game in Steam > right-click > **Properties...**
2. Go to the **Installed Files** tab
3. Select **Verify integrity of game files**

This will re-download and revert any files that REX/M2EX changed back to the original versions.

### Mod Compatibility
**All mods should be compatible with REX & M2EX.**

There may be minor glitches with certain mods, so check the [mod patches](https://discord.com/channels/1456826444360581235/1501929819204616363) channel on the Discord Server for any recommended fixes.

<Aside type="caution">Do not try running mods without following this guide. The default launchers that many mods come with **will not work**, and should only be used for changing mod configuration options.</Aside>

### Installing Mods
You can install mods as per the mod's instructions, either by dropping the files into the folder or using an installer (for mods which provide one). 


### Running Mods
<Tabs syncKey="game">
  <TabItem label="Medieval 2">
    Check the mod is located like below:

    <FileTree>

    - `Medieval II Total War` Your Medieval 2 folder that contains M2EX.exe
      - mods
        - modfoldername For example "Tsardoms-3.0". Make sure this doesn't contain any spaces!
          - ... 

    </FileTree>

    <Aside>There are two main methods detailed below. The first one is recommended, because it ensures any options in the mod's config file are used.</Aside>

    #### Batch File method
        1. Download [the pre-made .bat files](../../downloads/REX_M2EX_mod_batches.zip).
        2. Extract `M2EX mod launcher.bat` to your M2EX installation directory (You can rename this .bat file if you like).
        3. Open the file with a text editor (e.g. Notepad). You should see:
          ```
          start M2EX.exe @mods\MODFOLDER\MOD.cfg
          ```
        4. Replace `MODFOLDER` with the exact name of your mod folder.
        5. Inside the mod folder, locate the mod config file, for example `Tsardoms-3.0.cfg`. In the .bat file, you need to replace `MOD.cfg` with the name of the mod config file.
        6. Save the .bat file

    #### Shortcut method
      1. Make a shortcut to `M2EX.exe`
          - On Windows 11, right-click `M2EX.exe`, then select **Show more options** and **Create shortcut**. You can place the shortcut wherever you want.
      2. Go to Properties on the shortcut, and set Target to: `"C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Medieval II Total War\M2EX.exe" --features.mod=mods/modfoldername`
           - Ensure the first part of the above path reflects where you have M2EX installed.
           - Set `modfoldername` to the name of the mod folder
           - Remember - if the mod folder of the mod you want to play has a path like here (main Mods folder->your mod folder->your mod folder) ⁠newcomers-help⁠ then you need to target the last one
  - You may also use Launch Options in Steam to run mods (e.g. `--features.mod=mods/modfoldername`). You can add M2EX as a non-Steam game as many times you want and rename it, adding different launch arguments for different mods.

    You can also launch mods in the terminal with `./M2EX.exe --features.mod=mods/modfoldername`
  </TabItem>

  <TabItem label="Rome">
    Check the mod is located like below:

    <FileTree>

    - `Rome Total War Gold` Your Rome folder that contains REX.exe
      - mods
        {/* TODO: Confirm and document correct mod locations. */}
        - modfoldername For example "**fatw**". Make sure this doesn't contain any spaces!
          - ... 

    </FileTree>

    <Aside>There are two main methods detailed below. You can use either.</Aside>

    #### Batch File method
        1. Download [the pre-made .bat files](../../downloads/REX_M2EX_mod_batches.zip).
        2. There are three batches depending on which version of Rome your mod runs on:
           - `REX mod launcher.bat` is for mods running on vanilla Rome.
           - `REX-BI mod launcher.bat` is for mods running on Barbarian Invasion.
           - `REX-ALX mod launcher.bat` is for mods running on Alexander.
        3. Extract the appropriate .bat to your REX installation directory (You can rename this .bat file if you like).
        4. Open the file with a text editor (e.g. Notepad). You should see a bit that says `-mod:MODFOLDER`.
        5. Replace `MODFOLDER` with the exact name of your mod folder.
        6. Save the .bat file

    #### Shortcut method
        7. Make a shortcut to `REX.exe` 
           - On Windows 11, right-click `REX.exe`, then select **Show more options** and **Create shortcut**. You can place the shortcut wherever you want.
        8.  Go to Properties on the shortcut, and set Target to: `"C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Rome Total War Gold\REX.exe" -bi -mod:bi/modfoldername -show_err`
            - Ensure the first part of the above path reflects where you have REX installed.
            - If it's an Alexander mod you'd swap the `-bi` to `-alex`, and if it's a vanilla RTW mod you'd delete it entirely.
            - Set `bi/modfoldername` to the name of the mod folder
            - You may also use Launch Options in Steam to run mods (e.g. `-mod:bi/modfoldername`). You can add REX as a non-Steam game as many times you want and rename it, adding different launch arguments for different mods.
    
    You can also launch mods in the terminal with `./REX.exe -mod:modfoldername`
  </TabItem>

<Aside>Before reporting an issue, use the troubleshooting checklists below.</Aside>

#### Troubleshooting Checklist
- Make sure you have exactly followed the [Installation guide](../installation/) on a clean installation of the game(s).
- Check you are using the latest **Stable** release. Not a Test release.
- Check you have installed REX/M2EX in the main game folder (not the `/mods` folder).
- If you are running your game in any other language than English - try the latter and see if it helps.
- Check your game files have not been flagged as a false positive by an antivirus. For testing purposes only, you can check if disabling smart screen or UAC helps.

#### Troubleshooting Checklist - Mods
If you are running mods, *also* check the below:
- Make sure you have carefully followed the [Running Mods](../running-mods/) guide.
- Check your mod running methods for any typos (happens to the best of us) and that they're pointing correctly to REX/M2EX.
- Check the [mod patches](https://discord.com/channels/1456826444360581235/1501929819204616363) channel and apply any fixes for your mod.
- Check if you have installed a mod requiring installation outside the `/mods` folder (e.g. into the main directory) - if yes then M2EX won't work. If you want to play with M2EX with some other mod, you may need to delete the game directory and re-install it.
- Have non-REX/M2EX users reported bugs with this mod in the mod's forum or on Discord? Some mods may have issues even when played with the vanilla game, and it might not be an issue with REX/M2EX.

#### "My game is running poorly" checklist
- When you have both an integrated GPU and a dedicated GPU, ensure the latter is being used.
- Ensure you are not using any "Extreme" graphics settings.
- Reduce or disable MSAA, as this is very demanding.
- If playing a mod, ensure that logging in the mod's configuration file is set to `info` instead of `trace` (look for `.cfg` in the mod directory):
![Setting the log level to info in a mod configuration file](../../../assets/log_level_fix.png)
- Obviously if you have 100 Chrome tabs open, this will have an effect on performance. Try closing any other demanding applications.
- Sometimes using V-Sync or capping the FPS can help the feeling of an unsteady frame rate (and take some strain off your PC).

#### I have no sound in battles
If you are experiencing no sound during the battle - make sure it's not you hitting the ALT + S hotkey which the game uses for muting (including in vanilla).

## Reporting issues
If you have gone through the troubleshooting checklists and nothing helped, check the steps below to prepare a bug report:

#### Logs
Get the logs right away after the bug happens so you can attach them later. You need to send logs for *all issues*, even if your game didn't crash to desktop.

- Normal logs are in the main folder, called `system.log.txt`. Grab this file *immediately*, as it's overwritten every time you run the game.
- For crashes only: Crash logs are saved in your game directory in the `reports` folder. Please send the latest `.txt` file only, not the `.dmp` files, alongside the `system.log.txt`.

If you do not have any reports or a `system.log.txt`, at least try to show where you crashed, error window contents and if possible send a save file.

#### Preparing a report
Describe what is wrong and when it happens (in preparation for posting). A video + a message describing it would be the best option, but you can upload a screenshot and/or simply just write a text description. Be precise and give as much detail as possible. If you got a error message – show it! 

Before you report, if at all possible, try replicating the issue. For example, if you have a button missing in your campaign, start a new one and see if the bug persists. Or try exiting and going back into the game on the same save file/try a different save/try loading it again. 

#### Posting your report
Issues will often get lost in the general chat channels, so you should post them in:

- [⁠help-troubleshooting](https://discord.com/channels/1456826444360581235/1497355400402440355) – for any hard errors, crashes, very low FPS, options (camera etc.) problems and problems prohibiting you from playing the game and other emergencies that need a quick response. Sometimes you might be asked to copy that report and make a fresh post in the issues channel, or you might do that on your own if no one answers. 

- [⁠issues](https://discord.com/channels/1456826444360581235/1471288433816371282) – for anything else including things that aren't an emergency, bugged or broken functionality (e.g. missing portraits, units behaving in the wrong way) etc. The channel settings won't let you post there without proper tags, like vanilla + REX or modded + M2EX. Sometimes you need to mind what was already fixed or is it vanilla behaviour that belongs to suggestions channels.

A checklist for your report:
- Tag the post with which game this is
- Tag the post with whether it's vanilla or modded
- Specify which version of REX/M2EX you're using
- If using a mod, specify the mod and which version of it you're using. Ideally, check if the issue occurs in vanilla too.
- Detailed description of the issue and when it happened
- Supporting screenshots or videos
- Upload `system.log.txt`. If it's a very large file and Discord won't let you upload it, put it in a .zip file first. 
- Upload crash logs, if applicable

An example of a post in both channels could be, "Hi. I got an error while trying to recruit mercenaries. It happens when I click the 'pay' button. No error is visible on the screen. It happens all the time and in other campaigns that I am playing. Here is a video/screenshot/further text explanation. I've attached the logs. M2EX 21/06 version. I am running the mod SSHIP, version 0.98. This bug does not happen in vanilla."

Sometimes you will be asked for further actions after your initial post.

Normally every mount of a given type looks identical, so a cavalry unit is forty copies of the same horse. This feature lets a mount type list several models, and each horse (or camel, elephant, wardog, pig) picks one. It "stacks" with soldier variation: you can vary the riders, vary the horses, or both.

## Which name goes where

Three different name spaces are involved and it's kind of confusing:

1. `export_descr_unit.txt`'s `mount` attribute names a **mount type** from `descr_mount.txt` (`mount generals horse`).
2. The models inside a mount type name **battle model entries** (`descr_model_battle.txt`). These are single_word_names without spaces.
3. Those battle model entries in turn name skeletons and mesh/.cas files.

Variation lives entirely at level 2, inside the mount type. Unlike soldier variation, this does *not* change the EDU, and because every variant shares the one mount type, they all have the same gameplay values like the radius, mass and collision.

## The models block

The old `model` line in `descr_mount.txt` still works exactly as before:

```
type            heavy horse
class           horse
model           horse_heavy
radius          1.5
...
```

The new `models` block (note the `s`) lists a pool instead:

```
type            heavy horse
class           horse
models
{
    skeleton    horse_heavy
    horse_heavy horse_heavy_b horse_heavy_pink
}
radius          1.5
...
```

Each horse of this type is given one model from the pool. Ids are separated by spaces or newlines, up to 255 of them, and listing a model twice gives it double the odds.

`skeleton` is required. It names the battle model whose skeleton and scale applies: the animations, where the rider sits, and the collision scale, the same thing as `skeleton` in the `soldiers` block, and the same rule applies: it must exist in the DMB, but it does **not** have to appear in the pool. A skeleton-only model that never renders is fine. Note that it names a battle *model*, not a skeleton id, even though the keyword says skeleton.

## Animals

`descr_animals.txt` takes the exact same block:

```
type            wardogs
class           wardog
models
{
    skeleton    dog
    dog dog_black dog_spotted
}
radius          0.4
...
```

## A few things to know

- Every model in the pool must be rigged to the same bone layout as the `skeleton` model, or its animation comes out garbled. The game warns at load if a pool model declares a different skeleton.
- The scale comes from the `skeleton` model and affects collision. If a pool model has a different scale in its battle model entry, it will render at its own size but collide at the skeleton model's size. The game warns about this too i.e. probably don't do it.
- At sprite distance (the zoomout where units become billboards), all the mounts of a unit use the first pool model's sprite. Same deal as soldier variants.

Inside an event you already know which faction, settlement, or character it concerns: the attacker, the besieged town, whoever just moved. `local` and `target` are two new keywords that let you point at them directly, instead of hardcoding a name you already know. They work in every command and condition that takes a faction, settlement, or character argument, in both RTW and M2TW.

```
monitor_event GeneralAssaultsResidence TrueCondition
    set_faction_standing local target -0.5
end_monitor
```

In an event, `local` is the actor and `target` is the other side. For `GeneralAssaultsResidence` that makes `local` the attacking faction and `target` the defending one. Settlement arguments split the same way: `local` is the event's settlement and `target` the other settlement involved.

Characters only get `local`. No event tracks a target character yet, so writing `target` in a character argument logs an error and skips the line.

Outside an event, in the dev console or in scripts that run at game start, `local` falls back to whatever the UI has selected: your faction, the last settlement you clicked, the last character you clicked. `target` has no such fallback, so using it outside an event logs an error and skips the line.

Three things this doesn't help with:

- Regions have no shorthand. `freeze_recruit_pool` is the only command that takes a region, and no event tracks a current region, so there is nothing for `local` to resolve to. Name the region directly.
- Faction lists, like the `factions { ... }` block in `historic_event`, take a set of factions rather than one. `local` only ever resolves to a single faction, so it cannot fill a list. Use `all`, or list the factions explicitly.
- `sub_faction` inside `spawn_army` is read once, when the script file is first parsed, long before any event fires. `local` has nothing to resolve to that early, so it does nothing there.

Normally every soldier in a unit uses the same model, so a forty-man unit is forty copies of the same guy. This feature changes that in two ways: a unit can mix several models, picked at random for each soldier, and the model can change as the unit's armour is upgraded. Both work in RTW and M2TW.

The old `soldier` line in `export_descr_unit.txt` still works exactly as before:

```
soldier  roman_legionary  40  0  1.0
```

The model on the `soldier` line plays two roles. It picks the mesh rendered in battle, and it tells the engine which skeleton drives the unit - how fast it walks and runs, where missile fire spawns from, whether the primary weapon has a charge animation. If you add `armour_ug_models` (below), the per-tier entries swap the mesh; the skeleton stays as whatever was on the `soldier` line. So you can name one model on the `soldier` line for the skeleton and entirely different models in `armour_ug_models` for the meshes, if you have a reason to. Vanilla M2 did this for a handful of units.

The new `soldiers` block (note the `s`) lists several models, and each soldier in the unit is randomly given one of them:

```
soldiers  40, 0, 1.0
{
    skeleton  roman_legionary
    default
    {
        roman_legionary
        roman_legionary_var2
        roman_legionary_var3
    }
}
```

The numbers after `soldiers` mean the same as on the old line: count, extras, then optional mass, radius and height. Inside the block, `default` is the pool of models an un-upgraded unit draws from.

`skeleton` is required when you use the `soldiers` block. It names the model whose skeleton drives the unit — the same role the model on the old `soldier` line plays. The named model has to exist in `battle_models.modeldb`, but it does **not** have to appear in any of the mesh pools below; if you want a skeleton-only model that never gets rendered, that's fine. If the keyword is missing or the named model can't be found, the parser fails the unit loudly.

## Armour upgrades

Add `armour N` blocks to swap the model pool when the unit's armour is upgraded:

```
soldiers  40, 0, 1.0
{
    skeleton  legionary
    default  { legionary_a0_v1  legionary_a0_v2 }
    armour 1 { legionary_a1_v1  legionary_a1_v2 }
    armour 2 { legionary_a2_v1  legionary_a2_v2 }
}
```

A unit draws from the pool whose number matches its current armour upgrade level: no upgrades uses `default`, one upgrade uses `armour 1`, two uses `armour 2`. The pools are independent, so they don't need matching counts. `default` can list four models and `armour 2` just one.

There is also a shorter form, one model per tier and no per-soldier variation:

```
soldier           legionary  40  0  1.0
armour_ug_levels  0 1 2
armour_ug_models  legionary  legionary_a1  legionary_a2
```

The `soldier` line still drives the skeleton; `armour_ug_models` just swaps the mesh per tier. M2 has had this form for a long time; it now works in RTW too.

A few things to know:

- The `soldiers` block replaces the old `soldier` line, so don't also give the unit a `soldier` line or `armour_ug_*` lines. The parser reads whichever form comes first and chokes on the leftovers.
- Every mesh in the unit (the default pool and every `armour N` pool, or the meshes listed in `armour_ug_models`) needs to be rigged to the same skeleton as the model named on `skeleton` / `soldier`. If a mesh uses a different bone layout, its animation comes out garbled. The model itself can differ, it's the bone layout that has to match.
- M2 already varies soldiers within a single model through mesh variations. The `soldiers` block does something different: it swaps the whole model. The two stack, so the block picks which model a soldier uses and mesh variations then vary that model further.

Mounts and animals can vary the same way; see [Mount and animal variation](../mount_variation/).

The Total War map is a huge square. This normally suffices but this forces you to fill the entire map with provinces even if you don't want to, or you explicitly want to block some areas off. The usual trick for this was a "deep forest" province with a settlement buried somewhere unreachable, which still left a phantom city on the books with all the rebel, AI and territory bookkeeping that comes with it, confusing the campaign AI and still having rebels as their owner.

A **wasteland region** does all of this properly. Wastelands have no settlement, no owner, and no economy. The AI never targets it, it never counts towards a map-control victory, and no rebels or brigands spawn in it. Combined with the `impassable_shrouded` ground type (below), it becomes a black void that units cannot enter and players cannot see into. Both work in RTW and M2TW.

## Making a region a wasteland

A wasteland is defined in `descr_regions.txt` by writing the keyword `wasteland` where the settlement name would normally go. Because a wasteland has no settlement, owner or economy, the rest of the region body carries no meaning, so the entry can stop right after the map colour:

```
Sahara_Province
wasteland
80 40 20
```

The first line is the region's name key, which still has to exist in your `<campaign>_regions_and_settlement_names.txt` file. The keyword `wasteland` takes the place of the settlement name. The three numbers are the region's RGB colour in `map_regions.tga`. That is the entire entry.

```
Britannia_Province
londinium
romans_julii
britons_rebels
70 130 180
gold
0
2
```

You can also convert an existing region into a wasteland by swapping its settlement name for `wasteland` and leaving the remaining lines in place. Those lines (faction, rebel, resources, triumph, farm level) are still read but ignored, so the older long form keeps loading.

On the map side, paint the region's colour into `map_regions.tga` exactly as you would for any region. The one difference is that a wasteland does **not** need a settlement-position pixel, because it has no settlement.

## Terrain

By itself a wasteland region is still made of whatever terrain you painted in it, so units could in principle walk across it. To turn it into a proper black void, you paint its tiles with the `impassable_shrouded` ground type in `map_ground_types.tga`:

```
impassable_shrouded   RGB 32 32 32
```

A tile painted this colour is **impassable** (no land unit can move onto it) and **permanently shrouded** (it stays black under the fog of war forever, so the player never sees what is there). That combination is what gives a wasteland its empty, off-the-edge-of-the-world look.

There is a related, visible option if you want a barrier you can still see:

```
impassable_land       RGB 64 64 64
```

`impassable_land` blocks movement the same way, but it stays visible: the player sees the terrain, it just cannot be crossed. Use `impassable_shrouded` for hidden void and `impassable_land` for a visible wall like an impassable mountain range. Both ground types now work in RTW as well as M2TW.

`impassable_shrouded` is not tied to wasteland regions. You can paint it inside a normal faction's region to wall off an unreachable, unseen corner without making the whole region ownerless. The region keeps its settlement and owner; those particular tiles are just dead and dark.
